newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CAVALIER RHODES LIFTS SOUTH AFRICA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAVALIER RHODES LIFTS SOUTH AFRICA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Spectacular late order hitting marshalled by Jonty Rhodes boosted South Africa to a comfortable 46-run win over Australia in their third one-day international at Newlands on Wednesday.
South Africa took a 2-1 lead in the seven-match series after Rhodes' undefeated 83 from only 77 balls carried them to 245 for eight after his side had been deep in trouble at 106 for five.

In reply Australia struggled to 199 all out after being reduced to 25 for four as three wickets fell in four balls of the eight over. They were further hampered by the absence of opener Mark Waugh who injured a hand in attempting a slip catch and was unable to bat.
Even so Australia might have stood a chance but for South Africa's explosive finish to their innings.
Rhodes shared a 70-run sixth wicket partnership with Natal team mate Derek Crookes to get the recovery back on the road before they were parted at 176 for six.
But a 40-run partnership in five overs with Shaun Pollock (21 in 15 balls) and 23 runs in 10 balls with Rudi Bryson (17 not out in seven balls) lifted South Africa to undreamed of heights.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne came in for some heavy punishment, being hit for three sixes as his last three overs went for 40 runs. He ended with figures of two for 64 in 10 overs.
Australia lost Greg Blewett in the fifth over but the game effectively ended in the eighth.

Stuart Law was caught behind off paceman Bryson for four, Steve Waugh had his off stump uprooted for a first ball duck, and two balls later Michael Di Venuto was run out for 13 by a direct hit on one stump from Jacques Kallis.
A 69-run partnership between Michael Bevan (82) and Ian Healy, standing in as skipper for the resting Mark Taylor, merely prolonged the agony for Australia.
The fourth match in the series is in Durban on Saturday.
